prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a conceptual educational explainer illustration embedded in a GitHub research report, landscape format.
Primary request: Explain the central idea of BCAP to a researcher at a glance. BCAP adds a soft penalty to the critic loss when the critic's slope with respect to its input is too large, checked on BOTH real and generated samples. It does not clip gradients and the penalty updates only the critic.
Style: polished hand-drawn educational infographic with crisp large typography, generous white space, white background, restrained teal/orange/navy palette, friendly simple icons and thin rounded arrows. Make it legible when reduced to about 850px wide.
Composition: title at top reading exactly "BCAP: discourage steep critic slopes".
Upper half: a simple data-flow diagram. One teal node labeled "Real samples" feeds a SINGLE shared navy node labeled "Critic". A separate orange branch labeled "Learned prior" points to "Generator" and then "Generated samples"; generated samples feed that SAME Critic. Real and generated samples are two input batches evaluated by the same critic, not separate critics.
From the shared Critic, show two clear outputs into a loss combination: "GAN loss" and "Slope penalty". They combine with a plus sign into "Critic update". Under Slope penalty put "Check real + generated inputs". Make clear both losses together train the critic. No arrows from the slope penalty to the generator or prior.
Lower half: two small intuitive conceptual curve cartoons, not a measured graph. Left: a smooth gentle critic response curve at a marked input point, a small tangent slope, green badge "Below threshold" and annotation "No penalty". Right: a smooth curve with a steep local tangent at a marked input point, orange badge "Above threshold" and annotation "Penalty grows with excess slope". Show steepness of the critic response curve, not a probability density or a gradient being cut off. These cartoons are schematic examples and do not depict training outcomes.
At bottom small but legible text: "A soft loss penalty. It changes the critic objective."
Constraints: mathematically faithful concept, correct direction of arrows, one shared Critic, distinguish real and generated sample colors, no quantitative axis ticks or numerical results, no invented thresholds, no formulas or equations (those appear as real mathematical markup in the report), no papers or URLs or logos, no extra safeguards, no clipping scissors or hard cutoffs, no claims about which experiments pass. Restrict text to the exact provided short labels. Use clean negative space and align the flow so crossings are avoided.
